name: Citizenship by Descent (Jus Sanguinis)

requirements.blocker_text: Code de la Nationalite Malienne, Article 8: a legitimate child born to a Malian father acquires Malian nationality automatically, regardless of birthplace. Since a 1995 amendment (Article 8-5), a child of a Malian mother and a foreign father also receives Malian nationality by default, with the option to repudiate it within six months of reaching majority. For a natural (non-marital) child, nationality follows whichever parent's filiation is legally established first; if the other parent is stateless or of unknown nationality, the child acquires Malian citizenship regardless.
requirements.fix_path: Establish the parental link to a Malian-citizen parent through a birth certificate and the parent's own citizenship documentation.

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative (NGO-hosted primary legal text) -- Code de la Nationalite Malienne (1962, as amended 1995), Article 8 descent provisions

STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an NGO-hosted copy of the primary legal text, tier 3 (this dataset treats citizenshiprightsafrica.org as tier 3 rather than tier 2, consistent with how it was classified for other African countries built earlier in this session, e.g. Burkina Faso); Mali's own Journal Officiel publication of the code, and any current Ministry of Justice guidance, were not independently located or fetched in this build -- disclosed gap, worth a dedicated retry. GENUINE FINDING: the 1995 amendment removing the old asymmetry (previously nationality passed reliably only through fathers) is real and dated -- prior to 1995, a child of a Malian mother and foreign father did not automatically acquire citizenship the way a child of a Malian father did. citizenship_after_months set to 0 to reflect automatic acquisition at birth (or at majority for the repudiation window, which does not change the acquisition timing itself). dual_citizenship_allowed left null: this source did not address whether Mali generally tolerates or requires renunciation of a second nationality acquired this way.
